title: FactorIA audio document (*.audio.json)
description: A non-destructive chain of steps over a sound: a WAV or OGG, a sound patch (`*.sfx.json`) or another audio document. `audio.render` applies the steps offline, `audio.bake` writes the result next to the document as a WAV or OGG; the same bytes on every platform. Errors name the file and the JSON pointer; docs/SOUND.md, "Audio documents", explains the format and `audio.info {}` lists the steps.

doc.description: What the sound is and where the game plays it.

source.description: Where the sound comes from: a project path (.wav, .ogg, .mp3, .qoa, .sfx.json or .audio.json), or an object that also picks the take and the note of a sound patch.

seed.description: An .sfx.json source: added to the patch's seed (another take of its noise).

note.description: An .sfx.json source: transpose the patch so its root pitch becomes this note, e.g. "C4".

seed.description: Picks the take of every random step (granular, an .sfx.json source).

format.description: wav (16-bit PCM) or ogg (the engine's Vorbis encoder).

channels.description: source keeps the source's channels; mono mixes down to one.

path.description: Project path bake writes, ending in .wav or .ogg as the format says. Leave out to bake next to the document.

steps.description: The chain, applied in order. At most 64.

trim.description: Cuts the sound to a part: from `start` to `end` (or `length` after `start`), in seconds. With `auto` it also removes the silence at both ends: everything quieter than `thresholdDb` before the first and after the last loud sample, keeping `padding` seconds of it. Use it first, so later steps and the loop work on the sound itself.

end.description: Seconds where the sound ends (default: its end). Not with `length`.

length.description: Seconds to keep from `start`. Not with `end`.

auto.description: Also trim the silence at the start and the end.

thresholdDb.description: auto: samples below this level (dBFS) count as silence.

padding.description: auto: seconds of silence kept at each end.

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

fade.description: Fades the start in and/or the end out over `in` / `out` seconds. `curve` shapes it: linear, equalPower (a quarter sine: constant loudness when two sounds cross), smooth (a half cosine: S-shaped), exponential (slow start: x squared), logarithmic (fast start). A fade out of a few milliseconds removes the click at the end of a cut.

in.description: Seconds of fade in at the start.

out.description: Seconds of fade out at the end.

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

normalize.description: Sets the level: `mode` peak makes the loudest sample reach `target` dBFS (default -1); `mode` lufs makes the integrated loudness (BS.1770, the measure assets.check_mix uses) reach `target` LUFS (default -16) but never lets the peak pass `ceilingDb`. Put it last, or after the steps that change the level.

target.description: dBFS (peak) or LUFS (lufs). Default -1 for peak, -16 for lufs.

ceilingDb.description: lufs: the loudest sample stays under this (dBFS).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

gain.description: Multiplies the level by `db` decibels (negative is quieter).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

pitch.description: Moves the pitch by `semitones` and keeps the duration (a time stretch and a resample, both written for this engine). Good to about +/-7 semitones for sound effects; beyond, voices and tones start to sound processed.

semitones.description: Semitones, -24 to 24 (12 is an octave up).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

stretch.description: Changes the duration and keeps the pitch (WSOLA). `factor` multiplies the length (2 is twice as long) or `seconds` sets the length. Noise and tones stretch well; sharp transients smear a little at large factors.

seconds.description: The new length in seconds. Not with `factor`.

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

speed.description: Plays the sound `factor` times as fast, so pitch and duration move together like a tape (2: half as long, an octave up).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

eq.description: An equalizer: low and high shelves, peaking bands and 12 dB/octave low-pass and high-pass filters (RBJ biquads).

freq.description: Centre or corner frequency in Hz.

gainDb.description: Boost or cut in dB (shelf and peak).

bands.description: 1 to 8 bands, applied in order. Each is {"type": lowShelf|highShelf|peak|lowPass|highPass, "freq": Hz, "gainDb": dB (shelf, peak), "q": 0.1-18}.

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

filter.description: A resonant filter (the synth's state-variable filter, 12 dB/octave): lowpass removes highs (muffles), highpass removes lows (thins), bandpass keeps a band. `to` slides the cutoff there over the whole sound (an exponential sweep, e.g. a riser or a filter-open on a song's master). `mix` blends the filtered sound with the dry one.

cutoff.description: Frequency in Hz where the filter acts.

resonance.description: Q: 0.707 is flat, 2 to 8 adds a whistle at the cutoff.

to.description: Slide the cutoff to this frequency (Hz) by the end of the sound.

mix.description: Share of the filtered sound (1: only the filtered sound).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

compressor.description: Reduces the dynamic range: above `thresholdDb` the level rises only 1 dB for every `ratio` dB. `attack` and `release` (seconds) say how fast the gain follows, `kneeDb` softens the corner, `makeupDb` brings the level back up. The detector looks at the loudest channel, so a stereo image does not shift.

thresholdDb.description: Level above which the compressor acts, dBFS.

ratio.description: dB in for 1 dB out above the threshold (1 = off, 100 = limiter).

kneeDb.description: Width of the soft knee in dB (0 = hard).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

distortion.description: Waveshaping distortion: `drive` multiplies the level into a curve (`mode` soft rounds the peaks like a tube, hard clips them flat, fold bends them back and sounds metallic) and `level` brings the loudness back down.

drive.description: Gain into the distortion: 2 is warm, 10 is crunchy, 50 is fuzz.

mix.description: Share of the distorted sound (1: only the distorted sound).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

bitcrush.description: Lo-fi: reduces each sample to `bits` bits and holds it at a lower sample `rate` (the sound of old consoles and samplers).

rate.description: Hold samples at this rate in Hz (default: the sound's own rate).

mix.description: Share of the crushed sound (1: only the crushed sound).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

reverb.description: Adds a room: the synth's reverb (eight damped combs and four all-passes). The sound is extended by `tail` seconds so the reverb can die away.

mix.description: Level of the wet signal added to the dry one.

damping.description: How fast high frequencies die: 0 bright, 1 dull.

size.description: Scales the delay lines: 0.25 small room, 4 hall.

tail.description: Seconds added after the sound (default: decay, at most 5).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

delay.description: An echo: the synth's feedback delay. The sound is extended by `tail` seconds so the repeats can die away.

feedback.description: Share of each repeat fed back (0.95 at most).

mix.description: Level of the echoes added to the dry sound.

tone.description: Low-pass in the feedback loop in Hz, 0 = off (darker repeats).

tail.description: Seconds added after the sound (default: until the repeats are 60 dB down, at most 8 repeats).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

reverse.description: Plays the sound backwards (a reverse cymbal, a suck-in before a hit).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

layer.description: Mixes another sound over this one: `source` is a WAV/OGG, an .sfx.json patch or another .audio.json. It starts `offset` seconds in, at `gainDb`, optionally moved by `semitones`. If it ends later than the sound, the sound grows. A mono layer on a stereo sound plays on both sides.

source.description: Project path of the sound to mix in.

offset.description: Seconds after the start where the layer begins.

seed.description: An .sfx.json layer: added to the patch's seed (another take of its noise).

note.description: An .sfx.json layer: transpose the patch to this note, e.g. "C4".

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

loop.description: Makes the sound loop without a seam. The part from `start` to `end` is the loop body; its last `crossfade` seconds are blended into its first ones, so when playback wraps from the end to the start the wave carries on. Whatever is before `start` is kept as an intro that plays once; whatever is after `end` is dropped. The loop points are written to the baked file's import settings (loopStart, loopEnd in assets.json), which AudioSource, audio.play and audio.music honour with loop on. Only gain and normalize may follow a loop step.

start.description: Seconds where the loop body begins (default 0).

end.description: Seconds where the loop body ends (default: the end of the sound).

crossfade.description: Seconds blended over the seam; at most half the body.

curve.description: equalPower suits unrelated material, linear suits the same wave.

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.

granular.description: Replaces the sound by a texture made of tiny grains of it (a rain from a click, a swarm from a vowel): each grain is `grainSize` seconds of the sound, Hann-windowed, and `density` grains start per second. The read position moves through the sound (see `scan`) with a random offset (`jitter`), each grain's pitch is moved up to +/-`pitchSpread` semitones. Seeded, so the same step always makes the same texture.

jitter.description: Random offset of each grain's read position, as a share of the sound, up to half of it either way (0 = none, 1 = up to half the sound before or after the scan position).

pitchSpread.description: Each grain is moved by a random amount up to this many semitones either way.

scan.description: How much the read position moves through the sound over the texture: 1 once from start to end, 0 stays in the middle.

start.description: Seconds where the part of the sound to read from begins.

end.description: Seconds where it ends (default: the end of the sound).

enabled.description: false skips the step without removing it.
